headline: Quest Diagnostics confirms data breach affecting patient personal and health data
summary: The cyberattack targeted Quest's Quanum lab testing system, which handles patient health records and billing data. The company is still investigating the full extent of the compromise.
details: Medical lab testing giant Quest Diagnostics has confirmed a cyberattack and data breach impacting sensitive patient information. The company disclosed the incident in an 8-K filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

Quest learned of the attack on Wednesday, which targeted its Quanum lab testing system. Quanum is used by doctor's offices, hospitals, and healthcare practices to request lab tests and manage billing, storing extensive patient health and medical records.
The company stated that unauthorized access included "certain patient records." Quest has notified law enforcement and is actively investigating the scope of the breach.

This incident is the latest in a series of major cyberattacks affecting the healthcare industry this year. Healthtech companies have become prime targets for financially motivated cybercriminals seeking to steal sensitive data.

Quest has not yet specified when the breach began, whether a ransom was demanded, or the number of affected patients or healthcare customers. The Quanum system is utilized by approximately half a million clinicians across North America.
This marks Quest's second significant data breach in a decade, following a 2019 incident where 11.9 million patient records were compromised through a third-party billing company.

topic: Gemini AI Pro vs Plus value
headline_marked: [[Google One AI Plus offers better value]] than Pro for most users, despite recent downgrades
headline: Google One AI Plus offers better value than Pro for most users, despite recent downgrades
summary: Despite recent downgrades, Google One AI Plus still provides robust features like the Flash model and generation tools, with subtle differences in quality and speed compared to the Pro plan for most users.
details: Google has restructured its Gemini bundles, pushing casual users towards the Google AI Pro plan. However, one editor found that the cheaper Google One AI Plus tier might be the ideal sweet spot for most people, offering significant savings.

The recent overhaul of Google One plans, rolling out now, primarily benefits AI Pro subscribers. Pro users gain the Spark agentic model (now labeled Task), a perk previously exclusive to the Ultra tier.

Conversely, AI Plus is losing the Flash Pro model in November, meaning it will rely on an older version of Flash. Free users will be limited to the Flash Lite engine, indicating Google's strategy to encourage upgrades to higher tiers.

Despite these downgrades, AI Plus still offers a robust package for Android users. It retains the Flash model, along with generation tools for images, video, and audio clips, providing substantial computing power.

Testing revealed no significant difference in rendering speed for image and video generation between the Flash model versions. While subtle variations in quality exist, most users switching between Plus and Pro are unlikely to notice them easily.

The primary distinction lies in usage or token limits; Plus has lower caps, such as video generation being locked after five prompts until a 24-hour reset. However, these limits are generally sufficient for everyday use, unlike Pro's doubled allowance.

Google One AI Plus also maintains essential features like document and photo uploads, text prompts, voice commands, and integration with Notebooks, Gems, and Scheduled Actions. Users can also choose the AI's "Thinking level" (Low, Medium, High) for varied response thoroughness.

A key benefit for the author is the 2TB storage tier included with AI Plus, which is crucial for managing large Google Photos libraries and other Google apps. This provides ample storage headroom, a significant upgrade from the base 200GB option.
caption:
